title: Noise on the Record
transcript: Our building manager noticed that residents often waited until morning to email about noise. By then, they could rarely say exactly when it had started or stopped. During a trial, residents could open a short form on their phones and tap a button to record the current time. They selected where they heard the sound most clearly, such as beside the bedroom window. The manager compared reports across floors and traced one repeated late-night rumble to a loose panel in the garage. Once it was secured, the rumble stopped. The manager kept the form and added a space for residents to say whether the noise had woken them.

questions.prompt: What detail was often missing from the morning emails?
options: How many residents had heard the noise.
When the noise had started or stopped.
Whether the building manager had been called.
questions.answer: When the noise had started or stopped.
questions.explanation: 住户隔天早上才发邮件，往往记不清噪音开始或结束的确切时间。

questions.prompt: What did the reports from different floors help the manager discover?
options: The garage door was being used after closing time.
Some residents had entered the same report twice.
The sound was strongest in vacant apartments.
A building fixture was responsible for a recurring noise.
questions.answer: A building fixture was responsible for a recurring noise.
questions.explanation: 经理对照不同楼层的报告，发现反复出现的轰鸣声来自车库里一块松动的面板。

section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
